title: crossvalind
summary: Generate cross-validation indices and logical train/test partitions.
description: `crossvalind` provides MATLAB-compatible cross-validation split helpers for older Statistics and Machine Learning workflows. K-fold calls return numeric fold ids, while holdout, leave-M-out, and resubstitution calls return logical training/test masks.

signatures.label: indices = crossvalind('KFold', n, k)
signatures.description: Return a column vector of one-based fold ids for `n` observations distributed across `k` randomized folds.

signatures.label: indices = crossvalind('KFold', n, k, 'Classes', group)
signatures.description: Assign fold ids while balancing observations within each class label.

signatures.label: train = crossvalind('HoldOut', n, p)
signatures.description: Return a logical training mask after randomly holding out fraction `p` or count `p` for testing.

signatures.label: [train, test] = crossvalind('HoldOut', n, p)
signatures.description: Return complementary logical training and test masks.

signatures.label: [train, test] = crossvalind('LeaveMOut', n, m)
signatures.description: Randomly mark `m` observations as test observations and return train/test masks.

signatures.label: [train, test] = crossvalind('Resubstitution', n)
signatures.description: Return all-true training and test masks for resubstitution workflows.

examples.description: Create a reproducible holdout training mask.
Preserve class balance when producing a holdout split.

returns: `KFold` returns a numeric column vector with one-based fold ids in the range `1:k`.
`HoldOut`, `LeaveMOut`, and `Resubstitution` return a logical training mask by default.
Two-output partition calls return `[train, test]` logical column vectors.
notes: `crossvalind` consumes RunMat's shared RNG stream, so `rng(seed)` controls reproducibility.
`Classes` accepts numeric, logical, string, string-array, or character-row labels with one label per observation.
`Min` validates that each class has enough observations for class-balanced splits.

errors.when: The method, observation count, partition value, options, classes, or output count is invalid.
The requested output is too large or cannot be allocated.

gpu_residency: No. `crossvalind` is a small control-flow/index generation helper. GPU-resident inputs are gathered before partition generation, and outputs are host logical or numeric index arrays.
